question: Does a deterministic response projector fit once on all complete older target/control families remove the even/odd reverse-control instability on fresh text?
motivation: The even-fit projector flips one fresh paraphrase control at gain 1.0 while odd-fit does not. MLP and attention weight-function usage is task-typed, so arbitrary split-specific bases are a plausible estimator-instability source. Pooling is frozen before fresh evaluation and uses no optimized DAS or gain.
fit: Pool every older jointly capable temporal/is-was A1/A2 target row and both matched-control splits. Fit one rank-eight response projector per site and one rank-64 MLP input basis from all older A1/A2 training rows. No fresh row, outcome, gain, or threshold enters the fit.
evaluation: Run the frozen rank48 source graph in reverse on temporal-v13/iswas-v12 at gain 1.0 and on temporal-v13 paraphrase controls.

predictions.pred_a_authority_disjointness_finiteness: Authorities match, old fit rows and fresh evaluation rows are disjoint, support has 48 sites, all values are finite, and exactly 19 forwards execute.
predictions.pred_b_pooled_reverse_coordinates_transf: Every compiled response-site coordinate projection is at least 0.75, mean coordinate residual is at most 0.20, and worst coordinate residual is at most 0.20.
predictions.pred_c_pooled_reverse_behavior_passes: Temporal and is/was behavior projections are each at least 0.80 and worst target residual is at most 0.15.
predictions.pred_d_pooled_reverse_controls_are_selec: Control margin RMS is at most 0.10, median full-vocabulary KL at most 0.02, and top-one flip fraction is zero.
predictions.pred_e_pooling_resolves_the_split_failur: The pooled projector simultaneously exceeds the prior even-fit minimum behavior projection 0.7962746 and improves its 0.0625 flip fraction to zero.

decision: All five predictions establish a stable gain-one reverse interface under complete-family pooled identification. Failure closes projector pooling as a repair and preserves the rank48 program as forward/OOD sufficient but not uniformly reverse-selective.
